title: I'm 38. If You're in Your 20's or 30's, Read This.
author: Tim Denning
body:
Getting old sucks.

The one positive is that as we age, we mature. That’s been the case for me. Not much fazes me anymore.

I’ve been part of so much drama – personal bankruptcies, homeless friends, my battles with drugs and alcohol, nearly getting knifed to death, friends in jail, job losses, mental illness, \$1.2M theft, online trolling, going from entrepreneur to corporate to entrepreneur, etc.

I’m not that smart but these experiences have given me some powerful lessons to share to anyone in their 20s or 30s (feel free to forward it to them as well).

== *1. When you turn 35 you'll see the difference between those who took risks and those who didn't.*

How old you feel comes down to how you lived.

Not taking risks leads to regrets which ages you faster. You feel like you could have done more but you never do.

== *2. Having kids isn't the end of freedom, it's the beginning.*

People told me at 20 that having kids was bad. God, these people were so wrong. *I could die tomorrow now that I’ve met my daughter.*

Kids are hard but so are the best things in life. Choose your hard.

== *3. Chasing obsession is the fastest way to become a high performer.*

The only solution I’ve found is to go from being passionate to all-out obsessed with one thing. Hardcore obsession.

- They’re full of excuses
- Think short term
- Don’t invest in themselves
- Get sucked into a 9-5 job that leads nowhere

#quote[Let’s say that the person you love the most has just been shot. Either you will go about the task of seeing to those needs by learning a unique set of skills, _or the world will reject you_. – Jason Pargin]

== *4. Raise your standards so high people think you're a psychopath.*

People need good reasons *not* to chase their dreams and settle for second best.

== *5. Never follow the conventional path.*

We all sell ourselves a story. The key is to resist selling yourself the story that the conventional path is the right one. It sucks. Stop lying.

== *6. One of the clearest signs of intelligence is being able to hear an opinion you disagree with and not act emotionally.*

We can disagree with each other and still hug or be friends.

== *7. As you get older you'll want to leave your loser friends behind. It's normal.*

It’s okay to change friends. Just slowly reduce contact with the ones who you don’t vibe with anymore.

== *8. The more hard things you do the more successful you become.*

It feels amazing to do a hard thing and make it through.

== *9. No one who climbs the corporate ladder is happy. It's a trap. Choose freedom.*

If you want to be happier then get the hell off the corporate ladder.

== *10-20. Life lessons continued*

The life you dream of is built before and after work. Find a dark place. Be at one with it. Maniacs are incredible. Avoid being busy. Disappear from public life.

== *Money isn't evil.*

#quote[Romantic artists are the worst. So are \$0 hobbyists.]

The escape route is to obsessively learn how money works.

== *Shorter lessons*

- Turn off news and politics to naturally increase your IQ.
- Writing online is the easiest way to attract opportunities.
- Exercise every day, preferably in nature.
- Spend more time with your parents. Soon they'll be gone.

== *Understand human psychology and you can make as much money as you want.*

Key: humans act out of self-interest. Appeal to it.

title: The disappearing middle of software work
author: Karri Saarinen
body:
I think the center of software work is moving.

The middle of software work has been the most important part for a long time. You started with an idea, and eventually you shipped something, but almost all of the effort lived in between. Turning intent into something real meant opening the codebase, booting up the environment, and writing the code. That middle absorbed most of the time, attention, and craft of software teams.

My belief is that this is changing.

Pure coding agent workflows can now produce working code from goals, context, and tasks. They operate more independently, requiring you to touch the code less and rely on the IDE less. The IDE becomes more of a code viewer than a writing tool.

As these systems improve, this middle becomes thinner. Less time is spent manually translating intent into implementation.

What actually needs to be built is still the important question. Understanding the problem, gathering the right context from customers and internal teams, and shaping the work so it can be acted on effectively matters more because agents act directly on that input.

Design, in this sense, is not about artifacts or tools. It is about forming and shaping clarity of the intent through ideas, exploration, research, and discussion. It is about deciding what matters, what constraints apply, and what tradeoffs are acceptable. Good product work is seeking clarity.

In this era, directing and managing agent work becomes the craft. Writing code is less like constructing a solution and more like setting up the conditions for a good solution to emerge.

This is what we work on. The Linear workspace is the coordination and context layer for product work.

When the middle disappears or blends in, what becomes more in focus is the work of forming the right intent and making sure the outcome actually meets it.

title: How to fix your entire life in 1 day
author: DAN KOE
body:
If you're anything like me, you think new years resolutions are stupid.

Because most people go about changing their lives in the completely wrong way.

I want to share 7 ideas you probably haven’t heard before on behavior change, psychology, and productivity so you can do just that in 2026.

Let’s begin.

=== *I – You aren’t where you want to be because you aren’t the person who would be there*

If you want a specific outcome in life, you must have the _lifestyle_ that creates that outcome long before you reach it.

The bodybuilder has to grind to eat *unhealthily*. The CEO has to force themself to lie in bed past their alarm clock.

=== *II – You aren’t where you want to be because you don’t want to be there*

#quote[Trust only movement. Life happens at the level of events, not of words. – Alfred Adler]

All behavior is goal-oriented. It's teleological.

The lesson here is that real change requires changing your goals.

=== *III – You aren’t where you want to be because you’re afraid to be there*

The anatomy of identity:

+ You want to achieve a goal
+ You perceive reality through the lens of that goal
+ That behavior becomes a part of who you think you are
+ You defend your identity to maintain psychological consistency

=== *IV – The life you want lies within a specific level of mind*

The 9 stages of ego development:

+ *Impulsive* — No separation between impulse and action.
+ *Self-Protective* — The world is dangerous and you learn to look out for yourself.
+ *Conformist* — You are your group and its rules feel like reality itself.
+ *Self-Aware* — You notice you have an inner life that doesn’t match the exterior.
+ *Conscientious* — You build your own system of principles.
+ *Individualist* — You see that your principles were shaped by context.
+ *Strategist* — You work with systems while aware of your own involvement.
+ *Construct-Aware* — You see all frameworks as useful fictions.
+ *Unitive* — Separation between self and life dissolves.

=== *V – Intelligence is the ability to get what you want out of life*

*The mark of low intelligence is the inability to learn from your mistakes.*

To become more intelligent, you must:

- Reject the known path
- Dive into the unknown
- Embrace the chaos and allow for growth
- Become a deep generalist

=== *VI – How to launch into a completely new life (in 1 day)*

Three phases of identity flip:

+ *Dissonance* – They feel like they don’t belong in their current life.
+ *Uncertainty* – They don’t know what comes next.
+ *Discovery* – They discover what they want and make 6 years of progress in 6 months.

=== *VII – Turn Your Life Into A Video Game*

Your vision is how you *win*.

Your anti-vision is what's at *stake*.

Your 1 year goal is the *mission*.

Your daily levers are the *quests*.

All of these act as a concentric set of circles, like a forcefield, that guard your mind from distractions.

– Dan

title: Kingmake yourself
author: Yasser
body:
Kingmaking is when someone with influence anoints a winner. In the startup world, it happens when a tier 1 VC anoints a startup as the winner of an obvious category.

This is a very powerful idea. It's even more powerful when you can do this to yourself.

You do not need permission to act like the person you are trying to become. The behavior has to come first, and you have to maintain it long enough for reality to catch up.

=== *On Mamdani*

He never acted like his victory was unlikely. He never sounded like he did not belong. This is narrative design.

People root for you when they think you deserve more than you have got. They root against you when they think you have more than you deserve.

=== *The Blank Canvas*

You have an advantage that established players do not. No one knows who you are. It is a blank canvas and you get to draw anything.

Founders are narrative designers. Reality is perception. You can alter reality by altering people's perception.

=== *The Necessity of Delusion*

Kingmaking is delusional. You need to be delusional. Your chances instantly become much higher when you are delusional.

Any person you look up to is delusional. They did not become that person by accident.

=== *When the Lag Closes*

Reality is lagging behind actions because the effect of these actions takes time to show.

The moment the lag closes is when other people start correcting the narrative for you. This is how successful people become successful.

title: If you're still applying to jobs, read this
author: Tanay Kothari
body:
Companies don't hire the most qualified person. They hire who makes the decision feel easiest.

I've hired over 200 employees across three companies and reviewed over 100,000 resumes.

*But every now and then, someone does something different.*

*These people skip the line.* Not because they're gaming the system, but because they've already demonstrated the initiative I'm actually hiring for.

=== *Effort Comes Before the Application*

They focus on the outputs:

- Polished resume
- Optimized LinkedIn
- Practiced interview answers

But those are just *artifacts*. The application isn't the beginning. It's the reveal.

=== *1. The Builder*

*Primary differentiator: making things exist.*

They thrive on:

- Starting from scratch
- Working fast under pressure
- Turning ideas into something real
- Showing instead of telling

A 20-year-old shipped a fully functioning feature in one weekend. Thousands of lines of code. In 48 hours.

=== *2. The Analyst*

*Primary differentiator: understanding how things work.*

A teardown shows me exactly how someone thinks. It shows me what they notice, what bothers them, and what they'd prioritize.

=== *3. The Operator*

*Primary differentiator: making things happen.*

He started selling for us - as a stranger. Closed three enterprise deals. Then he reached out and said, "If I join you, I can do a lot more."

=== *Do what others can't.*

Standing out isn't about being louder. It's about showing up before you're asked.

Most people won't do this. Good. That's what makes it work.

You've already won.
